raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "bounding rectangle of the L-shaped domain",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4 names an L-shaped bracket but gives no bounding-box aspect ratio. The 64×64 image resolution in Sec. 3.1 does not explicitly establish physical cell dimensions.",
      "readings": [
        "Bounding width W equals bounding height H.",
        "W = 2H.",
        "H = 2W."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "L-shaped outline and corner cutout",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4 'Example designs' and the Fig. 4 caption identify a classic L shape without specifying its orientation, arm widths, or cutout dimensions; the outline is left to the unavailable figure.",
      "readings": [
        "Remove the upper-right quarter of a W×H rectangle, leaving arms of widths W/2 and H/2.",
        "Remove an upper-right rectangle of width 2W/3 and height 2H/3, leaving arms of widths W/3 and H/3.",
        "Remove an upper-right rectangle of width 2W/3 and height H/2, giving unequal arm proportions.",
        "Remove the lower-left quarter instead, leaving material along the top and right."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "absolute geometric scale and uniform out-of-plane thickness",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "No physical dimensions or thickness are supplied for Fig. 4. For a fixed normalized geometry and two-dimensional elastic formulation, these choices do not change the normalized optimal layout.",
      "readings": [
        "Use nondimensional bounding width W = 1 and unit thickness.",
        "Use W = 64 grid-length units and unit thickness.",
        "Use W = 1 and uniform thickness t = 0.1."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "downward point load on the right edge",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "The Fig. 4 caption specifies the right edge but gives no position along it. The missing figure would be needed to locate the point.",
      "readings": [
        "Apply the load at the lower endpoint of the right boundary segment.",
        "Apply it halfway along that segment.",
        "Apply it at the upper endpoint of that segment."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_magnitude",
      "entity": "downward point force",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Neither the Fig. 4 caption nor the compliance setup states the force magnitude.",
      "readings": [
        "F = 1 in consistent force units.",
        "F = 10 in the same units.",
        "F = 100 in the same units."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "excluded corner forming the L shape",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The dataset section discusses masks, but Fig. 4 is an out-of-distribution problem and its cutout implementation is not specified.",
      "readings": [
        "Remove cutout elements entirely from the elastic domain.",
        "Retain the full rectangular mesh and fix cutout densities to zero, retaining the stated E_min stiffness.",
        "Retain the rectangular design array but exclude cutout cells from both stiffness assembly and design updates."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "material adjoining the load and clamped edge",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The Fig. 4 setup does not state whether load and support attachment cells remain designable or are protected as passive solid regions.",
      "readings": [
        "All cells inside the L-shaped region remain designable.",
        "Fix a one-cell solid attachment region around the loaded node.",
        "Fix solid attachment regions at the load and a one-cell strip along the clamped edge."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "volume_fraction",
      "entity": "Fig. 4 material budget",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Equation (2) introduces the prescribed volume V0 without giving its Fig. 4 value. The training range [0.12, 0.5] does not identify this out-of-distribution instance's target.",
      "readings": [
        "Material fraction f = 0.20.",
        "f = 0.30.",
        "f = 0.50."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "volume_fraction",
      "entity": "reference area used to define the material fraction",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Equation (2) integrates over Ω, but the text does not establish whether Ω for this masked L-shaped example excludes the cutout or denotes the full rectangular grid.",
      "readings": [
        "Set V0 = f times the admissible L-shaped area.",
        "Set V0 = f times the full bounding-rectangle area, with the cutout contributing zero material."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "two-dimensional elastic constitutive model",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 3.1–3.2 give E0, E_min, and Poisson's ratio, but do not explicitly specify plane stress or plane strain. The cited 88-line code is not reproduced.",
      "readings": [
        "Use plane stress with the stated material parameters.",
        "Use plane strain with the stated material parameters."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "density-to-stiffness interpolation and penalization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The compliance setup references the 88-line approach but supplies no interpolation equation, penalization exponent, or continuation schedule. The explicit SIMP discussion later concerns fracture.",
      "readings": [
        "Use E(ρ) = E_min + (E0 − E_min)ρ^2 with fixed exponent 2.",
        "Use E(ρ) = E_min + (E0 − E_min)ρ^3 with fixed exponent 3.",
        "Use the same SIMP law with an exponent increased from 1 to 3 during optimization."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "ordering of cone filtering and volume-enforcing transformation",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3.2 specifies Equation (2) and a two-pixel cone filter without defining their order or precisely identifying the field passed to stiffness assembly.",
      "readings": [
        "Cone-filter the generated field first, then apply Equation (2) to obtain volume-constrained FEM densities.",
        "Apply Equation (2) first, then cone-filter its densities, choosing the bisection offset using the final filtered volume."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "cone-filter treatment at exterior and cutout boundaries",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 3.1–3.2 state the cone shape and radius but do not define padding, boundary normalization, or whether masked cells participate in filter averages.",
      "readings": [
        "Truncate the cone at the L-shaped boundary and renormalize over admissible cells.",
        "Filter over the bounding rectangle, including fixed-zero cutout cells, and renormalize only at the rectangle boundary.",
        "Zero-pad exterior and cutout regions and retain the full cone normalization."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "relationship between the 64×64 design representation and analysis mesh",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3.1 fixes image and network resolution at 64×64 but does not explicitly state the Fig. 4 FEM mesh or whether each pixel is one analysis element.",
      "readings": [
        "Use one analysis element per design pixel on a 64×64 bounding grid.",
        "Use a 128×128 analysis grid with each design pixel assigned to a 2×2 element block.",
        "Interpolate the 64×64 density field onto a 128×128 analysis grid."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "finite-element interpolation and integration",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The compliance simulations are described as following the 88-line approach, without specifying element order or quadrature in the supplied text.",
      "readings": [
        "Use bilinear four-node quadrilaterals with 2×2 Gauss integration.",
        "Use four-node quadrilaterals with reduced integration and hourglass stabilization.",
        "Use biquadratic nine-node quadrilaterals with 3×3 Gauss integration."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial density field for the Fig. 4 MMA baseline",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The compliance sections do not specify MMA initialization. Uniform-density initialization is stated later for the separate fracture experiment.",
      "readings": [
        "Start from a uniform density satisfying the volume constraint.",
        "Start from a feasible, spatially perturbed density field.",
        "Start from a feasible nonuniform field biased toward connecting the load to the support."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "MMA update controls",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3.1 says MMA uses default hyperparameters without identifying an implementation or specifying move limits and asymptote controls.",
      "readings": [
        "Use a density move limit of 0.20 and initial asymptote half-width of 0.50.",
        "Use a density move limit of 0.05 and initial asymptote half-width of 0.10."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "postprocessing of the thresholded Fig. 4 designs",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3.2 references the simplest thresholding strategy from [66] without supplying its rule; the Fig. 4 discussion explicitly compares thresholded results.",
      "readings": [
        "Set densities at or above 0.5 to solid and the rest to void.",
        "Choose a density threshold that preserves the prescribed material fraction.",
        "Assign solid material to the highest-density cells until the target discrete material count is reached."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
